A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OC-Flow research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. The supplied material supports a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-manipulation, conditional molecule-generation, and peptide-design experiments, including appendix ablations and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendices D–E.

M1.justification: The additive-control framework, Euclidean and SO(3) updates, adjoint/VJP computation, and asynchronous scheduling remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 retain the same procedures; notation edits do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same face-editing tasks, six QM9 molecular properties, and PepFlow peptide-design scenarios. Appendix datasets, prompts, and evaluation subsets are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main and appendix experiments, including D-Flow and FlowGrad on QM9, the image-editing baselines, and PepFlow and Naive-SO(3) in peptide evaluations.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E retain the same splits, sample counts, metrics, optimizers, and budgets, including 100 image Euler steps, 50 molecular Euler steps, and 200 peptide simulation steps with 10 control terms.

E4.justification: The regularization comparison in Table 4, translation/rotation ablations in Table 5, optimizer ablation in Table 11, and Naive-SO(3) comparison in Table 12 already appear in v2 and are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run Rosetta averages for stability and affinity and controlled initial noise across reruns in Appendix E.3. No changes to repeated-run counts, uncertainty intervals, or significance reporting were found.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Tables 2–5 and 8–12 and qualitative examples in Figures 2–4 are unchanged. For example, OC-Flow retains image LPIPS 0.207 and CLIP 0.302, and combined translation/rotation peptide MadraX energy −0.263.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1.2 replaces its displayed control-integral bound with an expected terminal-distance-plus-control-energy bound, matching Proposition 1 already stated in the main text. Separately, v3 Equation 110 drops the factor C present in v2 Equation 38, creating an inconsistency with v3 Equations 16 and 129, which retain C. These are localized mathematical-statement changes, not new theorems.

C1.justification: Introduction contribution 2 now explicitly describes the running-cost KL guarantee as concerning joint distributions, whereas v2 referred generically to distributions. This qualifies the headline guarantee; the remaining core contributions and performance claims are retained.

C2.justification: The detailed interpretations of regularization, optimizer effects, and rotation guidance remain unchanged. Section 6 retains the computational-cost limitation and the same proposed extensions.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository availability statement and link in the abstract. The hardware, implementation settings, hyperparameters, and evaluation instructions in Appendices D–E otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to D-Flow, FlowGrad, E-MSA, and prior manifold-generation methods are unchanged. Citation-format edits do not introduce new related work.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammar and terminology corrections, changes the publication header, adds an internship footnote, and corrects computational-efficiency references from Appendix C.7 to Appendix D. The narrative and section organization remain substantially the same.

P2.justification: v3 systematically numbers and reformats displayed equations and adjusts spacing and page flow around existing material. All four figures and twelve tables retain their substantive visual content and organization.

improvement.justification: The added code location, clearer joint-KL claim, corrected Appendix C.1.2 bound, and repaired appendix references modestly improve accessibility and consistency. The missing C in Equation 110 introduces a localized defect, but the C-dependent form remains in the main statement and proof conclusion. This limits the gain without outweighing the documentation improvements; the method and experimental evidence remain unchanged.
